conclusion: Eli Stone is the most likely responsible party for the missing prototype. Evidence shows: (1) Eli stated he needed the prototype at 17:00 per D03_messages, establishing motive; (2) Service camera footage V04/V10 shows Eli with the prototype in service corridor at actual time 18:14 (camera timestamp 18:19 plus 5-minute offset from D03); (3) Access log D01 confirms Eli entered via service door at 18:14; (4) Schematic V01 shows service corridor provides unmonitored access to lab; (5) Timeline is consistent - prototype was in lab at 18:00 (V02), missing by 18:18 (V05), giving Eli window from 18:14-18:18 to enter and remove it; (6) All other staff members were accounted for elsewhere during critical window; (7) Eli's witness statement claiming he did not approach lab after 18:00 is contradicted by camera evidence.

exhibits.relevance: Establishes prototype location at 18:00 in lab before disappearance
Shows Eli Stone with prototype in service corridor; timestamp corrected to 18:14 using +5 min offset
Confirms prototype missing from lab by 18:18
Shows unmonitored service corridor link to lab enabling access
Access log confirms Eli entered via service door at 18:14
Establishes Eli's stated need for prototype and documents camera offset

alternative_explanations.explanation: Someone else accessed lab through unmonitored service corridor
alternative_explanations.reasoning: No other staff had opportunity; all others were documented elsewhere during critical window
D03 explicitly states coat descriptions are from shift assignments, not biometric identity; visual evidence V04/V10 clearly shows orange coat matching Eli Stone

limitations: Cannot definitively prove intent beyond reasonable doubt without additional corroborating evidence
Camera footage quality may limit detailed observation of actions
No direct witness testimony from lab interior during incident
